Each hit calls the same functions the microphone does, so a sketch written for the microphone reacts to the machine as it is. Once a sketch has started the machine, defining kickDetected() no longer opens the microphone on the first click (a sketch that reads micLevel still asks, and then both call it). Patterns. 'four on floor', breakbeat, 'half time', latin, sparse, your own startDrums({ kick: 'x...x...x...x...', snare: '....x.......x...', hat: 'x.x.x.x.x.x.x.x.' }) (a lane left out is silent), or one line of rhythm (below). The card. The lanes are named in the page's language (大鼓 小鼓 鈸 拍手 in a Chinese browser), the bar it is in shows beside the tempo, and the step that sounds is a yellow column (13:1 against the dark card, readable on a projector). Where the grid sits. At the top centre: on OpenProcessing between the 🎹 and OPC's icon and clear of the console, and below the 🎹 panel while that is open. – folds it, × stops the machine, and 🥁 in the 🎹 panel opens and closes it with no code at all. 🥁 brings the grid up stopped: tick its play box to hear it (a sketch's own startDrums() plays at once). The kit. @openav/drums' synthesized kit (no samples), heard from the first click like sound; the callbacks run from the start either way. On time, however heavy the sketch. The hits are handed to the kit ahead of time, on its audio clock: a heartbeat in a Web Worker wakes every 25 ms and schedules what falls in the next 0.1 s at its exact time. Measured on the kit's own output with a draw() that keeps the page busy 30 ms a frame, the kick-to-kick interval varies by 0.000 ms (0.5, which…

jsCopy Any text that is not a pattern name is a line of rhythm; names, grids and numbers work exactly as before. The line shows over the grid, and the word that sounds lights up and fades. writemeanse.g. a worda drum: bd kick, sd snare, hh hat, oh open hat, cp clap, rim, lt mt ht toms, cr crash, rd ride, cb cowbell"bd sd bd sd" ~a rest"bd ~ sd ~" spacethe words share the bar evenly"bd hh sd hh" [ ]a group shares one place"bd [sd sd]" *nn times in that place"hh*8" ,another line on top"bd*4, hh*8" < >one per bar, in turn"<bd*4 [bd ~ bd ~]>" (k,n)k hits spread over n steps"bd(3,8)" The whole list is in @openav/pattern, loaded from next to oav-p5.js with the drums. Drums the grid has no lane for (crash, ride, toms, open hat) get a row of their own; a hit off the sixteen steps (a triplet) is drawn where it falls inside its step. A mistake in startDrums("…") shows a card in the page's language with the character it is at, why, and how to fix it, and the machine plays 'four on floor' meanwhile; 'x...x...' on its own (one lane of the grid) says to put it inside { kick: … }. A line copied from strudel.cc works too: startDrums('s("bd*4, [~ sd]*2").fast(2)') plays [bd*4, [~ sd]*2]*2. s("…"), sound("…"), with ", ' or ` quotes, several of them ($: s(…)) as layers, .fast(n) and .slow(n); setcpm(110/4) or setcps(…) sets the tempo when startDrums() is given none. .bank("…") is left out (OAV plays its own synthesized kit) and anything else in the chain (.jux(rev), .every(…), .gain(…)) gets a card that says OAV does not do it yet and points at Open in Strudel; the rest plays. The way of writing one line of rhythm comes from TidalCycles / Strudel (strudel.cc); OAV implements it independently from their public documentation.

records.n: The cells and the line edit each other
records.x: Since 0.7 the line over the grid is always there (a preset shows the line its grid is: 'four on floor' is bd*4, [~ sd]*2, hh*8) and both ways work: Click a cell: the line is rewritten the way a person would write it, and the machine plays the new line at once. Steady hits become bd*4 / hh*8, one hit per group [~ sd]*2, a Euclidean rhythm bd(3,8) (with its rotation: bd(3,8,2) starts two steps later), anything else beat by beat: bd [~ ~ ~ bd] bd*2 ~. Lines are joined with , . When the line holds more than sixteen steps can (triplets, < >, /2, ?, bd:2), the first click shows a card saying what would go, and the next click rewrites it. Type in the line: click it, change it; Enter, or a pause of 400 ms, plays it and the cells follow. A mistake marks the word in red, a card says what is wrong, and the last line that worked keeps playing (not 'four on floor'). Escape drops what is not played yet. Typed keys never reach the sketch's keyPressed(). ↶ on the card (or ⌘Z / Ctrl+Z after touching the card) goes back one line; OAVp5.drums.history lists them. Copy puts startDrums("…", 110) on the clipboard, ready to paste into setup(). Open in Strudel opens the same line at strudel.cc in a new tab, as s("…") with setcpm(bpm/4) (one OAV bar is one Strudel cycle of four beats; strudel.cc's docs: setcpm(bpm/bpc)). OAVp5.drums.strudelUrl is the link. jsCopy OAVp5.drums.src is the line that plays, OAVp5.drums.edit("…") plays a line as if typed, OAVp5.drums.undo() goes back. Keys that swap the rhythm, step back and open Strudel: p5/examples/rhythm-lab/.

The card is part of the page, not the canvas, so a recording never shows it. drawRhythm() draws the rhythm on the canvas: jsCopy drawRhythm(x, y, w, h, style, options): style is 'grid', 'circle' or 'spiral'; a hit lights up the moment it is heard (the clock drumPhase reads) and a triplet sits where it falls. Options: colors ({ kick: '#f66', … }, any p5 color), color (one for all), off (the empty steps), playhead (a color, or false), bg, bars (spiral). Drawn inside push() / pop() with p5's own shapes, in 2D and WEBGL, p5 1.x and 2.x; in WEBGL (0, 0) is the middle of the canvas: drawRhythm(-width / 2, -height / 2, width, height, 'circle'). With no box it draws a strip along the bottom ('grid') or a square in the middle. A sketch with all three: p5/examples/rhythm-visual/.

The drum machine is also the clock: sixteen steps a bar, counted from startDrums(). Declare what happens at which bar: jsCopy call / read / define cue(bar, name, every)at bar bar (1 is the first, 4.5 is halfway through bar 4); every bars again if given cueNamethe last cue that fired ('' before the first) cueFired(name, bar)a cue's bar has come barStarted(bar), stepStarted(step, bar)the first step of every bar; every step The same cue() twice adds nothing, so it may also sit in draw(). On one step the cues fire in the order they were declared, then barStarted, stepStarted and that step's hits. A silent clock: startDrums({}). The whole of it, ready to open: p5/examples/drums/; a line of rhythm with drumPhase and beatPhase: p5/examples/rhythm/; the rhythm drawn on the canvas: p5/examples/rhythm-visual/.

records.n: Values over time: lag, env, speed, spring, trail
records.x: A knob or micLevel jumps; what looks good is how it moves between the jumps. TouchDesigner does this with CHOPs; the same operators are here, one call each in draw(), nothing to declare, and seconds are seconds (the same curve at 30 and at 144 fps): jsCopy TouchDesigneroav-p5 Lag CHOP (Lag 1 / Lag 2)lag(value, up, down)follows value: up seconds while it rises, down while it falls (down = up if left out; 0.1) Trigger CHOP (attack, decay)env('kick', attack, decay), trigger('boom')0..1: up to 1 in attack seconds after each event, back to 0 in decay (0.01, 0.3). Events: 'kick' 'snare' 'hat' 'beat' (the microphone or the drum machine, the hits kickDetected hears), 'note' (any key), 'bar' 'step' (the drums), a cue's name, trigger('boom'); or a switch: env(mouseIsPressed, …) Speed CHOPspeed(rate)adds rate every second: rotate(speed(TWO_PI)) turns once a second Spring CHOPspring(value, stiffness, damping)follows like a mass on a spring (100, 6: two or three bounces; damping 20: none) Trail CHOPtrail(value, seconds)the last seconds (2) as an array, 60 values a second, oldest first, the newest last Slope CHOPslope(value)how fast it changes, per second Count CHOPcount(beat), count(beat, 4), count('kick')how many times it turned on; with 4: 0 1 2 3 0 …; a name: how many of those events so far a CHOP's viewerscope(value, 'label')a small plot in the corner of the page (below) drawTrail(values, x, y, w, h)the same plot on the canvas, in the work and in a recording Seconds, the same as in TouchDesigner. A lag's seconds mean what a Lag CHOP's do: about the time the value takes to follow 90% of a jump, so lag(x, 0.1) here moves like a Lag CHOP set to 0.1 (Lag CHOP). Underneath it is a one-pole lag with a time constant of seconds ÷ 2.3 (ln 10); @openav/mapping's smooth keeps its own 63% time constant. Attack and decay are lengths in both. Nothing to declare. The first lag() in draw() keeps the first lag's memory, the second the second, every frame; spring(), speed(), trail() … are counted each on their own. Put one inside an if, or in a loop whose length changes, and the order slips: a card says so, and from then on oav-p5 matches each call by the line it is written on. The sure way is a name, a string at the end: lag(p.size, 0.1, 0.5, 'p' + p.id). A named one is the same wherever it is called, draw(), setup() or mousePressed(); an unnamed one outside draw() has nothing to remember by and returns its input (speed 0, trail []), and a card says that too. env(), trigger() and count('kick') are about events and work anywhere. A sketch with its own speed or count keeps it;…

records.n: Recording: a video with its sound
records.x: jsCopy call / read / define startRecording(), startRecording(seconds), startRecording({ seconds, fps, mic, name, canvas, bitrate })record the canvas and the sketch's sound; with seconds it stops by itself; a take is 5 minutes at most. canvas is the canvas to record (a p5 canvas or createGraphics(); the default is the biggest p5 canvas on the page), bitrate is bits a second (the default follows the canvas size and frame rate: 4 to 16 Mb/s, up to 24 Mb/s above 30 frames a second) stopRecording()stop; the file downloads recordingIsOnwhether a take is running recordingSaved(info)the file is saved: name, seconds, bytes, format, width, height, audio, sources, warnings, blob, url In the 🎹 panel, ⏺ starts and stops a take with no code; while it runs, the 🎹 button shows a red dot and the time (a click on the dot stops it). 📷 saves the canvas as a PNG. What is in the video. The p5 canvas at its own pixel size (a retina screen doubles it), 30 frames a second, and every sound this file makes: startSound(), the drum machine and the pads, the microphone while it is on, and p5.sound 1.x, mixed into one track while the speakers play as before. The 🎹, the drum grid, the cards and OPC's panel are not on the canvas, so they are not in the video. The file. MP4 (H.264 + AAC), which Instagram, YouTube and every editor take, wherever the browser can write it: Chrome 126 and later, Edge, Safari. Elsewhere (Firefox, an older Chrome) WebM, and a card says Instagram will not take it. It is named oav-20261015-183005.mp4; on a computer it lands in Downloads, on a phone a Share button on the card saves it to the photo library or sends it to Instagram. Checked after every take. A card says what was recorded (format, length, size, with or without sound) and, when something is wrong, what and why: nothing reached the recording although a sound was on (no click on the page yet, nothing played), WebM, an almost empty file, a black video of a canvas that was not black (Safari recording a WebGL canvas, WebKit 229611), an image from another site on the canvas (no CORS), no recorder in this browser. The microphone is in the take while it is on: wear headphones, or the speakers are recorded twice. record=nomic leaves it out. p5.sound. p5.sound 1.x (the one for p5 1.x) is recorded. The p5.sound made for p5 2.x connects each sound straight to the speakers, with no output a recording can tap: it is not in the take, and a card says so. Switch the sketch to p5 1.11, or use startSound() and startDrums(). Sound the sketch makes with its own Tone.js or Web Audio code is not recorded either.…

inputhow a real controllerWeb MIDI in Chrome, Edge and Firefox; the browser asks once the on-screen controller🎹 opens <oav-controller>, which follows the controller you plug in a phone📱 in that panel shows a QR code; the phone's remote page MIDI tab plays the sketch All three arrive as the same MIDI bytes, so the sketch cannot tell them apart (midi.last.source can). Safari and iPad have no Web MIDI; the on-screen controller and the phone still work there. A sketch that uses Web MIDI itself (navigator.requestMIDIAccess, WebMidi.js) also hears the screen and the phone, as one more input called OAV Virtual MIDI. Other programs are a fourth input (0.7). What a program plays into OAV Virtual MIDI's output — Strudel's .midi('OAV Virtual MIDI') — reaches the sketch at the moment it was stamped with (midi.last.source is virtual-out); an external MIDI clock moves drumPhase, drumBar and a drum machine; and link=<room> brings another tab's or another computer's programs into this sketch. All of it: With Strudel.

Nobody watches OpenProcessing's console while playing, so problems are said on the page: a small card beside the 🎹, never over the middle of the canvas, in the browser's language, once per page, with a × to close it. Each card says what happened, why, and what to press, and the console gets the same sentence. The microphone: refused (the lock left of the address → allow → click the canvas), refused by the computer's settings, by an embed without allow="microphone", missing, held by another app (Zoom, OBS), an http: page, or the browser still asking. MIDI: no Web MIDI (Safari, iPad: use the 🎹 or a phone), or the permission refused. Only for a sketch that plays from MIDI; a sketch that uses none of this never sees a card. Your own code: an error inside notePressed(), kickDetected(), drumHit() and the other callbacks shows the message with the file and line, and the sketch keeps running. A sketch that declares its own note or knob1 (let, var, function) keeps it, and the card says what to read instead (midi.last.note, knob(1)). Sound and drums: waiting for the first click, the piano still loading (the electric piano meanwhile), an instrument that failed (the fallback plays), Tone.js unreachable, the drum machine playing silently until a click. Recording: started (what it hears, how to stop), saved (format, length, size, sound), a take with no sound in it, WebM (not for Instagram), a black take, an almost empty file, a canvas with another site's image, no recorder in this browser. ?oav_hints=off (or window.OAV_P5 = { hints: 'off' }) keeps them in the console only; OAVp5.hints lists what was said. 🩺 Check-up. 🩺 in the 🎹 panel (or OAVp5.check()) shows the version, the page, the browser, the microphone, MIDI, sound, drums, recording (MP4 or WebM here, the last take), the wiring, the sketch's own names and the hints so far, as one card to screenshot, with a copy button and a link to the full device check.

Hydra has a loader of its own; the same file works there, and Hydra's arrow functions read the variables each frame: jsCopy jsCopy note, velocity, knob1 … knob8, fader1 …, pad1 …, drumStep and the 🎹 on-screen controller are there the same way. Hydra is not p5, so there are no notePressed() callbacks to define; subscribe instead: midi.on('notePressed', (note, velocity) => { … }) or OAVp5.drums.on('hit', (lane, velocity) => { … }) (each returns a function that unsubscribes). Checked against hydra-synth 1.4.0, the library the editor runs (p5/test/hydra-smoke.cjs).

Why prepend. p5's friendly-error checker reads the last <script> on the page as your sketch. Put first, this file is never mistaken for your code. Why one asynchronous line is enough. p5 starts global mode on the window's load event, and a script inserted while the page is loading holds load back until it has run, so knob1 already exists in setup(). When the line does not load (offline, a typo in the URL), code that reads knob1 stops with knob1 is not defined. Embedding a sketch elsewhere. OpenProcessing's own pages allow MIDI and the microphone in the sketch frame. The embed code it gives you does not: add allow="midi" to that <iframe> if the embedded sketch should hear a hardware controller, and allow="microphone" if it should hear the microphone. Options, MIDI-level access and tests: p5/README.md. Examples: p5/examples/particles/, p5/examples/opc/, p5/examples/mic/, p5/examples/keys/, p5/examples/drums/, p5/examples/rhythm/, p5/examples/rhythm-visual/, p5/examples/rhythm-lab/, p5/examples/record/, p5/examples/lag/, p5/examples/chop/, p5/examples/with-strudel/ and p5/examples/note-names/.

Strudel is a live-coding environment for music in the browser, a JavaScript version of TidalCycles. OAV is a separate program. The two run side by side the way two programs on a stage do: Strudel plays, and OAV brings what Strudel does not have — knobs on screen and on a phone, a microphone that is analysed, Web MIDI where the browser has none — and draws what Strudel plays in a p5.js sketch, on the same page or in another tab or on another computer. They meet through MIDI (OAV's virtual port, "OAV Virtual MIDI") and through the page's own variables (knob1, micLevel, drumPhase). OAV never loads or calls any of Strudel's code. Everything on this page was run on strudel.cc as a user runs it (its editor, Ctrl+Enter, its documented functions): p5/test/strudel-smoke.cjs does it again.

Strudel → settings → prebake, add one line at the end, save: jsCopy Single quotes. Strudel reads text in double quotes (and backticks) as mini-notation: a URL in double quotes is a [mini] parse error. Why the prebake. It runs before your code, also after a reload (about 2.5 s after the editor appears), so OAV is on the page before anything opens MIDI. If Strudel's midin() ran before OAV loaded, midin('OAV Virtual MIDI') gets nothing and says nothing: reload. 🩺 then shows "no program has asked OAV Virtual MIDI for MIDI". The line can also be the first line of your code. Options go on the line before it: window.OAV_P5 = { link: 'my-room' }. Strudel's share button puts the prebake into the link (with "share with patterns" ticked): whoever opens it gets OAV too. On strudel.cc OAV changes its manners. It does not ask for MIDI when it loads (hardware=click: Strudel's midin() asks). The 🎹 panel is a box in the corner, a third of the window high, so the code stays in view. One card says which names Strudel already has — note, velocity, beat are Strudel's functions, OAV leaves them alone — and what to read instead: OAVp5.last.note, OAVp5.last.value, OAVp5.mic.on('beat', fn). knob1, micLevel, drumPhase and the rest are free names there.

records.n: Recipe 1: knobs, a phone and the microphone as Strudel's parameters
records.x: Strudel's signal() turns a function into a parameter; OAV's names are plain values a function can return. jsCopy knob1 moves with knob 1 of the 🎹 on screen, of a MIDI controller, or of a phone (🎹 → 📱, scan the code). knob(2), fader1, pad1 are there too. Measured: knob 1 at 0, the kick is silent; at 127, it is heard (RMS 0.58). Strudel reads the value when it schedules, 0.2–0.3 s before the sound: a knob is heard that much later. micLevel, bass, mid, treble are OAV's analysis of the microphone (Strudel has none); reading one asks for the microphone. Wear headphones: the microphone hears the speakers, and gain(signal(() => micLevel)) feeds back. Strudel's own MIDI input works on OAV's port too, also in Safari (no Web MIDI there; OAV's port is virtual): jsCopy Knob 1 of the on-screen MiniLab 3 is CC 74. midikeys('OAV Virtual MIDI') makes the 🎹 keys and the phone Strudel's keyboard.

records.n: Recipe 2: Strudel plays, a p5 sketch draws
records.x: On the same page. Send to OAV's port: jsCopy Strudel hands each note over 0.21–0.32 s early with the moment it should sound; OAV waits for that moment and then calls notePressed(note, velocity) (in Strudel, with no sketch: OAVp5.on('notePressed', fn)), moves knob1 for a CC, plays a pad. Measured on strudel.cc: each note is heard within 5 ms of its timestamp (10 notes, at most 4.5 ms late; p5/test/strudel-smoke.cjs), and drumPhase follows Strudel's clock to 0.1 ms. What arrives on the port is never handed back to OAV's input, so midikeys('OAV Virtual MIDI') played into .midi('OAV Virtual MIDI') is one echo, not a loop. Strudel's clock. MIDI counts 24 clocks a beat, so a cycle of one 4-beat bar sends 96: jsCopy drumPhase, beatPhase, drumBar, drumStep and drumBpm follow it. A drum machine started with startDrums() plays at Strudel's tempo, on Strudel's downbeat, and starts and stops with it (the card says "following an external clock · 128 BPM"). Measured at 128 bpm: drumPhase within 1.2 ms of Strudel's bar (median 0.04 ms), every kick within 6 ms of Strudel's beat (three runs); Strudel's start, which arrives three times with one timestamp, counts once. Without a clock nothing changes; clock=off ignores one. In another tab, or on another computer. Give both pages the same room. In Strudel's prebake: jsCopy and in the p5 sketch (OpenProcessing: before the one line; or ?sketch_oav_link=my-room on the page's address): jsCopy Everything Strudel sends to OAV's port — notes, CCs, the clock — reaches every other OAV page in the room, through the same relay the phones use. 🎹 grows a 🔗: green when another page is there; the panel says the room, the pages and the trip. The receiving page plays each note when Strudel plays it, not when it arrives: it lines the two clocks up from the fastest trips it has seen and the round trips both pages measure (packages/relay/link.js explains how), and Strudel's quarter-second head start covers the trip. Measured with two tabs on one Mac over wss://remote.cheyuwu.com (one way ≈ 61 ms): notes within −3 … +7 ms of Strudel's timestamps (two runs). Across two computers add the difference between the two halves of a round trip (usually a few ms). Keep the default relay (wss://): Chrome does not let strudel.cc reach a relay on your own machine or network (ws://127.0.0.1… is blocked by its local-network checks). On a network whose jitter is longer than Strudel's head start, linkdelay= (ms) buffers more. A page never sends on what it received, and a program that plays a linked note back out is caught as an echo. The room is the phones'…

records.n: Recipe 3: Strudel, Hydra and OAV on one page
records.x: With OAV in the prebake: jsCopy Hydra turns once a bar on Strudel's clock (through drumPhase), knob 1 drives Hydra and Strudel at once, and the microphone colours the picture.

Set before the line (window.OAV_P5 = { … }), or ?oav_key=value on a p5 page's address. keyvaluesdefault linka room name (letters, digits, -, _): pages in it hear each other's programsnone linkdelaymilliseconds of extra buffer on a linked page's notes0 clockfollow (an external MIDI clock moves drumPhase and the drums) · offfollow strudelauto (strudel.cc, or Strudel's functions already on the page) · on · offauto compacton (the panel as a box in the corner) · offon in Strudel hardwareauto · click · offclick in Strudel

Strudel is © its contributors (begun by Felix Roos and Alex McLean), free software under the GNU Affero General Public License v3: strudel.cc, source at codeberg.org/uzu/strudel. TidalCycles, whose way of writing patterns Strudel carries to the browser, is Alex McLean's. Music you make with Strudel is yours (Strudel's FAQ). OAV is MIT-licensed and a separate program. It contains no Strudel code, does not load @strudel/* at run time and calls none of Strudel's functions: it only looks at the page's address and at which names the page already has, to choose its manners. The two meet the way two programs on a stage meet, over MIDI. OAV's own rhythm strings (startDrums("bd*4, hh*8"), @openav/pattern) are an independent implementation of the TidalCycles / Strudel way of writing rhythm, from their public documentation. Please do not ask Strudel's community for help with OAV: OAV's issues are on GitHub.

Phones and iPads can be controllers: their motion sensors, a piano, and a TouchOSC-style control panel that grows from the world's params. Three packages do it, each usable alone: packagerole @openav/relaya zero-dependency WebSocket relay with rooms, and its browser client @openav/surfacethe control-surface widgets, the layout JSON, autoSurface(params) @openav/remotethe phone app (tabs 感測 sensors · 琴鍵 keys · 控制台 control · MIDI) and the show-side adapter To the mapper, a phone is one more input: it publishes signals, and routes connect them to params.

Run node serve.js on the show machine. It serves the pages and hosts the relay at /relay; nothing else is needed. Open a show that declares modules: { remote: true }, for example http://localhost:8080/examples/08-remote-surface/. The join card at the top left of the stage shows the URL a phone should open, with the show machine's LAN address filled in (the page asks serve.js for it at /__info) and the room: http://<lan-ip>:8080/packages/remote/?room=default. Open that URL on a phone on the same network. The card counts connected phones. The card also draws a QR code of that URL: point a phone's camera at it.

There is no serve.js there, so no relay of its own. A show that declares modules: { remote: true } uses the public relay (wss://remote.cheyuwu.com/relay) instead, and the card says so (public relay). Open example 08 on the computer, scan the QR code with the phone, and the phone's faders move the show. The room is random (show- plus 10 characters), made once and kept in this browser's localStorage, so a reload keeps the same room and two visitors never share one. A room name declared in the show (room: 'main') is ignored here for that reason; ?room=class-7 in the page URL always wins, which is how a classroom puts everyone in one show. ?relay=wss://your.host/relay uses a relay of your own (the phone link carries it along); ?relay=off turns the remote off for that page. The choice is pickRelay() in @openav/remote/relay-pick: this machine or its LAN (localhost, 192.168.x.x, *.local…) keeps the same-origin /relay and works exactly as before; any other host gets the public relay. The public relay has no accounts and no authentication. The room name is the only secret, so treat the QR code like one: whoever scans it can drive that show. Don't put it on a slide you share.

/packages/remote/ is a single page with a status header (connection, latency, room, the phone's id) and tabs: 感測 (sensors): a tilt ball, acceleration and rotation readouts, a multi-touch pad, knocks (a sharp jolt of the phone), and light from the front camera. iOS needs a tap on 開始 (start) before it gives motion data. 琴鍵 (keys): a piano that is one row of about three octaves in landscape, and two stacked rows in portrait (the upper row continues the range). Vertical position on a key sets velocity; hold-to-sustain and octave buttons included. 控制台 (control): a control surface. Its layout comes from, in order: the ?surface=<layout.json url> query, the ?meta=<json url> query (its params go through autoSurface), whatever the show publishes over the relay, and finally a small generic panel so the page is never blank. MIDI: a virtual MIDI controller, the same one the show displays (MIDI controllers & embedding). querymeaning room=<name>the room to join (1–32 characters of A–Z a–z 0–9 _ -; anything else means default) tab=sense|keys|control|midithe tab to open first surface=<url>a layout JSON for the control tab meta=<url>a JSON file with a params array; the control tab becomes autoSurface(params) relay=ws://…a relay somewhere else than the page's own server (the QR code on the join card carries it when the show uses the public relay) Each phone keeps a short random id in localStorage; it is the <id> in phone/<id>/….

iOS Safari only gives motion sensors and the camera to pages served over https://. Touch, keys and the control surface work over plain http:// on the LAN. For tilt and knocks on an iPhone, reach serve.js through an HTTPS tunnel and open the tunnel's address on the phone; the relay follows the page's origin (wss:// on HTTPS pages). Android Chrome behaves the same for the camera.

modules: { remote: true } in createShow() (or mountRemoteHost() from @openav/remote/host) does five things, so the world stays ignorant of phones: joins the relay as the room's runner (the show); files every phone signal into signals, and mirrors phone/<id>/… to phone/any/…, which always holds the value from whichever phone sent it last; builds the control surface: world.surface if the world ships a layout, otherwise autoSurface(world.params); and publishes it to every phone, including phones that join later; adds the surface/… → param routes to the mapper (skipping pairs that are already there); sends param values back to the phones about 10 times a second, so faders follow the timeline and other controllers. modules.remote optiondefaultmeaning room?room= in the page URL, else 'default'the room name auto{}options for autoSurface (pairs, meters, style, perPage, smooth, title) surfaceworld.surfacean explicit layout (wins over the world's) feedbackHz10how often param values are echoed relaychosen by pickRelay()'wss://host/relay' for a relay of your own, false for no remote. Without it: same-origin /relay on this machine or LAN, the public relay on a static host. ?relay= in the page URL overrides it urlthe samealias of relay (and the option mountRemoteHost() takes: it appends role, room and id) Routes for sensors are written at author time with the phone/any/… alias, because nobody knows a stranger's device id in advance (example 08): jsCopy show.remote is the host: { relay, layout, routes, bindings, room, publish(), frame(dt, state), connect(), dispose() }.

A surface turns fingers into named, normalized signals. Every widget publishes under surface/<page>/<id>; when the widget's range is not 0..1, the unscaled value also goes out as …/raw. typepublishesnotes fader<id>orient: v, h or auto (follows the cell's shape) · double-tap resets to def knob<id>grab the rim to turn, the middle to drag encoder<id> (phase, wraps) and <id>/delta (turns)endless button<id> 1 / 0momentary; a pulse param fires on the rising edge toggle<id> 1 / 0 xy<id>/x, <id>/y, <id>/downspring: true returns to the centre bank<id>/1 … <id>/Ncount, labels; one finger paints across channels radio<id> = index / (n − 1), raw = indexoptions: [...] pads<id>/hit pulse { pad, row, col, vel }, <id>/<n> velocity while heldrows, cols (default 4 × 4), labels; n counts from 0; velocity = where you hit (top soft, bottom hard) keyboardmidi/note/on, midi/note/off, midi/cc/64the same names a hardware keyboard uses number<id>− / + buttons (hold repeats) and a field text<id>, a string pulseEnter or ↵ sends label, meternothingdisplay only; fed by surface.feedback(name, value) Common fields: id, type, label, min, max, def, step, unit, color (cyan amber magenta lime violet coral white), and target (a param key, or an array for xy and bank) for hand-written layouts. The phone keyboard's notes are { note, vel, velocity, ch: 1, device: 'surface' }.

A layout is data, like a route: shareable as a file, writable by an agent, publishable by a world. jsonCopy Phones get turned, so a page decides its arrangement like this: if the page has a portrait or landscape variant for the current orientation, use its grid (widgets missing from its place keep their base spot or fill free cells); otherwise, if the base grid already has the right shape, use it; otherwise auto-reflow: the same widgets, repacked row by row into half (portrait) or double (landscape) the columns. Rows are a count, not pixels, so the grid always fills the screen and nothing ever scrolls. Widgets without x/y are packed into free cells with a default size per type. validateLayout(layout) returns a list of problems (empty = fine); new Surface() throws with that list on a bad layout.

autoSurface(params, options) turns a world's params into a layout, the routes that drive the params, and the bindings for feedback: jsCopy How each param becomes a widget: paramwidget pulse: truebutton step: 1 and a range of 1 (two values)toggle step: 1 and three to seven valuesradio (labels from options, else the numbers) a pair listed in pairsone xy pad driving both anything elsea fader when there are six continuous params or fewer, knobs when there are more surface: { type, color, label } on the paramwhatever it says Options: pairs, meters (params to also show read-only), style ('auto', 'fader', 'knob'), perPage (default 8; a page that scrolls is a page that fails), smooth (default 0.04 s on continuous routes, to hide 30 Hz network steps), title. Each param group gets its own page.

Give a widget a target and routesFromLayout(layout, params) writes its route (the same shape autoSurface produces): xy maps x to the first target and y to the second, bank maps channel i to the i-th target. A world can carry its layout as world.surface; the show side then uses it instead of generating one.

Every control reads CSS custom properties on :root (THEME_VARS: --oav-bg, --oav-surface, --oav-accent, --oav-radius, --oav-touch-min (44 px) …). Override them to re-skin the whole surface. The rules: dark, ≥ 44 px touch targets, the live number always visible, pressed = border and glow in the widget's color, navigator.vibrate where it exists. @openav/surface also exports phone helpers: lockViewport() (no scrolling or zooming), keepAwake() (Wake Lock), toggleFullscreen(), canFullscreen(), haptic(ms).

Clients connect to ws://<host>/relay?role=controller|runner|monitor&room=<name>&id=<device>. A room is a name; peers in different rooms never hear each other. fromtowhat controller (a phone)runner + monitorsignal and batch runner (the show)monitorsignal and batch runnercontrollers + monitorsfeedback (meters, fader echo), config (the surface layout; replayed to phones that join later) monitornobody Messages are JSON: {"type":"signal","name":"phone/ab12/tilt/x","value":0.3,"t":…,"pulse"?:true}, {"type":"batch","items":[…]}, ping/pong, status (peer counts), feedback, config. Clients ignore types they do not know. When the runner leaves, the room forgets its config. Messages over 256 KB are ignored, frames over 1 MB close the connection, and a phone that stops answering pings (screen locked, Wi-Fi gone) is dropped within about 40 s. jsCopy Continuous values are re-sent once a second so a phone that joins late, or a show page reloaded mid-performance, is never stuck on stale defaults. Pulses are never batched or repeated: a note-on delivered twice is a bug. The client reconnects by itself (0.5 s, doubling up to 5 s). fileSignal(signals, name, value, { pulse }) is the receiving half of the wire format: it declares a name the first time it is heard (signalMeta() knows the ranges of phone/…, surface/… and midi/… names), fills in whichever velocity spelling a note message lacks (vel 0..1 or velocity 1..127), then pulses or sets. To run the relay without serve.js: node packages/relay/server.js [port] (default 7458, health at /health), or attach it to your own Node server with attachRelay(server, { path: '/relay' }) from @openav/relay/server.

records.n: The show page on a phone
records.x: When the show itself runs on a phone, it can read the phone's own motion sensors without a relay. localSensors(signals) publishes the same names under phone/local/…, mirrored to phone/any/…, so routes written for "the latest phone" work either way. Call .start() from a tap (iOS permission rules): jsCopy

The relay has no authentication. Anyone on the same network who knows the room name can join as a controller and move your params. For a show, use a closed network or a room name nobody will guess. On the public relay the room is random and lives in the QR code; it is a convenience for trying a show, not a lock.

Signals are the single currency of the input layer: named, normalized, source-blind. This page lists every signal published by the built-in input packages. Conventions: ranges are 0..1 unless noted pulse signals fire events; their value is the event payload y axes are flipped where it makes performance sense (1 = raised), never raw pixels <n> is a number, <ch> a MIDI channel 1..16, <id> a device id, <slug> a device name made URL-safe

Every hardware message publishes the legacy names and the per-channel names. signalkindrangemeaning midi/note/onpulse{note, vel, velocity, ch, device}key down: vel 0..1, velocity 1..127, ch 1..16, device = port slug midi/note/offpulse{note, ch, device}key up midi/cc/<n>continuous0..1controller n (any channel) midi/bendcontinuous-1..1pitch bend (any channel) midi/ch/<ch>/cc/<n>continuous0..1controller n on one channel midi/ch/<ch>/note/<n>continuous0..1velocity while note n is held, 0 on release midi/ch/<ch>/bendcontinuous-1..1pitch bend on one channel midi/ch/<ch>/pressurecontinuous0..1channel aftertouch midi/ch/<ch>/poly/<n>continuous0..1polyphonic aftertouch on note n With two or more MIDI inputs connected, each device also publishes under its slug (from the port name: Arturia MiniLab 3 → arturia-minilab-3, duplicates get -2, -3): signalkindrangemeaning midi/<slug>/note/onpulse{note, vel, ch}key down on that device midi/<slug>/note/offpulse{note, ch}key up on that device midi/<slug>/cc/<n>continuous0..1controller n on that device midi/<slug>/bendcontinuous-1..1pitch bend on that device On-screen controllers (modules.midi.controllers) publish one name per control, midi/<device>/<control> (for example midi/minilab3/knob1), plus /hit pulses for pads and /raw values. They are listed in MIDI controllers & embedding.

The on-screen piano, QWERTY playing and the simulated performer publish the legacy note names with a smaller payload: signalkindrangemeaning midi/note/onpulse{note, vel, ch: 0}key down (vel 0..1) midi/note/offpulse{note, ch: 0}key up

signalkindrangemeaning chord/consonancecontinuous-1..1harmonic consonance of last gesture chord/countcontinuous0..10notes in last gesture chord/rootcontinuous0..127lowest MIDI note of last gesture chord/eventpulsefull analysis{notes, count, root, vel, pcs, consonance, isConsonant, isDissonant, isTriad, thirdsFraction, dissonanceLevel, chordType} chordType: single · major · minor · sus2 · sus4 · dim · aug · maj7 · min7 · dom7 · halfdim7 · maj9 · min9 · dom9 · six · min6 · cluster (very dissonant pile) · chord (anything else). Inversions resolve to their root-position name via pitch-class rotation. dissonanceLevel: 0 none · 1 mild (storm warning — foreshadow) · 2 severe (true cluster — commit to the decay language). Born from a real audience note at the IRCAM × C-LAB performance in Taipei: "dissonance detection wasn't strict enough."

Per-hand pinch distances = four precise continuous controllers across two hands. Normalized by palm size, so distance to the camera doesn't change your pinch. signalkindrangemeaning hand/left/present right/…continuous0/1hand visible hand/left/x /ycontinuous0..1palm position (y: 1 = raised) hand/left/pinch/indexcontinuous0..1thumb-tip ↔ index-tip (0 = touching) hand/left/pinch/middlecontinuous0..1thumb-tip ↔ middle-tip hand/left/spreadcontinuous0..1index-tip ↔ pinky-tip spread (hand/right/* mirrors the set. L2 mapping · values over time, the way TouchDesigner's CHOPs shape them: Lag, Trigger (envelope), Speed, Spring, Trail, Slope, Count. Pure logic, no clock of its own: every step is told the seconds that went by and is solved exactly over them, so 30 fps and 144 fps draw the same curve. What the parameters mean follows Derivative's TouchDesigner documentation; the code is OAV's own. In a p5 sketch, oav-p5 gives these one call each: p5 one line. exportsignature approachapproach(current, target, seconds, dt) → one step of a one-pole lag; seconds = time to 63% of a change (the smooth of @openav/mapping, which steps with it) Lagnew Lag({ up = 0.1, down = up }) · step(input, dt, up?, down?) → output · reset(v?): up while rising, down while falling (Lag CHOP's Lag 1 / Lag 2), in TouchDesigner's seconds (about 90% of a change) envelopeenvelope(times, t, attack = 0.01, decay = 0.3, peak = 1) → the Trigger CHOP's level at t for events at times (seconds, oldest first): a straight attack (0 → peak), then 0 after exactly decay; a retrigger starts where it is · envelopeStage(elapsed, attack, decay, from, peak) Speednew Speed() · step(rate, dt) → position: rate per second Springnew Spring({ stiffness = 100, damping = 6 }) · step(target, dt) → position (velocity alongside): a mass on a spring pulled to the input, solved exactly · springStep(x, v, target, k, c, dt) → [x, v] Trailnew Trail({ seconds = 2, rate = 60 }) · step(value, dt) → the last seconds, 60 values a second plus the newest, oldest first, fixed length Slopenew Slope() · step(value, dt) → change per second Countnew Count({ threshold = 0.5 }) · step(on, limit = 0) → times it turned on, looped to 0 … limit − 1 with a limit · wrapCount(total, limit) TD_LAG_RATIO, DEFAULTSMath.LN10: two kinds of seconds. Lag and lag() take TouchDesigner's Lag CHOP seconds (about the time to follow 90% of a change), so lag(x, 0.1) moves like a Lag CHOP set to 0.1; underneath, Lag divides by TD_LAG_RATIO (2.3) to get its time constant. approach(…, seconds) takes that time constant itself (63% of a change, what @openav/mapping's smooth always meant); the defaults above jsCopy

Worlds are visual code, and coding agents are good at code. A person describes a performance ("a jellyfish world that blooms on consonant chords"); an agent writes the world inside a chassis that already handles MIDI, mapping, timeline, console and backstage. This chapter is what an agent needs to do that well.

Continuous control goes through params; discrete events may use signals. Never read signals.get(…) in update() for something that varies continuously. Declare a param and let a route connect the signal to it. The shell never knows the work. Never edit packages/* to make one example look right. A framework change must make every work better. The reasoning is in Core concepts.

AGENTS.md at the repository root is the briefing: what the framework is, the two rules, how to create a new work, how to verify changes, and the conventions (vanilla ESM + JSDoc, no build step, no runtime dependencies, comments that explain the performance reasoning (why a knob feels right) rather than syntax, path-style signal names declared with signals.define).

The repository ships a Model Context Protocol server: packages/mcp/server.js, zero dependencies, JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio, one JSON message per line. Claude Code picks it up from .mcp.json when you open the repository. Other clients: jsonCopy It answers initialize (server openav 0.1.0, echoing the client's protocol version, 2024-11-05 if none is given), tools/list and tools/call. Results come back as one text item; objects are JSON-encoded. A failing call returns a JSON-RPC error with code −32000 and a message. toolargumentsreturns list_examplesnone[{ dir, title, summary }]: each example's folder, the <title> of its index.html, and the first comment line of its main.js read_docdoc (required): architecture, writing-a-world, signals, show-control, roadmap, agents, readmethe Markdown text. agents is AGENTS.md, readme the README; the others are docs/<name>.md scaffold_worldslug (required, kebab-case), donor (default 01-hello-particles){ created, next_steps }. It reacts to the on-screen piano or QWERTY keys: no hardware required. Space plays the timeline and something evolves. Report the URL, the params (what to map to knobs), the scenes, and the signals the world listens to.

cheyuwu-lab runs sketches in plain <script> pages, so it builds a classic-script bundle of each OAV package it wants. Instead of a hard-coded list, the lab's generator (tools/lab-dev/build-modules.mjs) scans packages/*/package.json and builds every package that declares a "lab" field (an object, or an array when one package yields several modules). No declaration, no module. keymeaning moduleoutput name, runtime/modules/<module>.js (lowercase, digits, -) kind"build" (default, bundle the code) or "declare" (only announce a module the lab implements itself) filessource files to bundle, relative to packages/; relative imports between them are resolved, JSON imports are inlined exportsnames exposed on window.OpenAV wireoptional file (relative to the package dir) run inside the module scope; lab is window.lab. It plugs the package into lab.signals / lab.params autowireone sentence on what the wiring does (goes into the lab's oav-manifest.json) remoteTaboptional {id, label, icon, entry}: adds a tab to the phone /remote app sinceversion or month Rules: relative imports only, no runtime dependencies, no build step in OAV itself. The generator is idempotent and has a --check mode (exit 3 = OAV has something new to regenerate).

records.n: Single source of truth: controllers and inputs live here
records.x: Decided 2026-10-03: every controller and input module the lab uses is written in OAV and reaches the lab only by reference: generated: runtime/modules/<module>.js from a "lab" declaration (header // GENERATED by tools/lab-dev/build-modules.mjs); served as-is: the lab's dev server serves /remote from packages/remote/index.html and /oav/packages/* from this repo. That covers the message format (relay/signals.js: signalMeta, fileSignal, velocity normalization), the virtual Web MIDI (midi/virtual-access.js), controller profiles and panels (packages/midi), the phone page (感測 · 琴鍵 · 控制台 · MIDI: packages/remote, packages/surface, packages/keys), phone sensors on the run page itself (localSensors, lab module motion), audio, sound, mapping and OSC (the OSC bridge is packages/osc/bridges/osc-bridge.js). To change one, change it here, test it here, push main; the lab regenerates (its nightly tools/oav-sync/sync.sh, or node tools/lab-dev/build-modules.mjs by hand) — never by editing the lab's copy. The lab is not allowed to grow a second copy. Its gate (node tools/lab-dev/modules-gate.mjs, also a test and the first step of npm run deploy) fails when a runtime/modules/*.js lacks the GENERATED header (a short, reasoned allow-list excepted — empty today) or when runtime/modules/ has a sub-folder (hand-copied packages). What stays in the lab is the thin host layer — code that must exist before a sketch loads or that only knows the lab's own pages: runtime/lab.js (the lab object, its relay socket, and the few lines that swap navigator.requestMIDIAccess for a lazy loader of the generated midi module), /remote's room picker (runtime/remote-room.js: which lab works are open) and its recording panel (runtime/rec-remote.js: the lab's own capture/record API), and the dev server's relay and routes. A new kind of controller or input never starts there.
Real problems, found in rehearsals and in the code, with what to do about them.

records.n: The console shows a ws://…:7457 error
records.x: Every show made with createShow() tries to stream to the backstage monitor at ws://<the page's host>:7457. When no monitor is running, the browser logs the refused connection. This is expected and harmless: the page retries with a growing delay (about 5 s, rising to 30 s) instead of spamming. To make it go away, run the monitor: bashCopy Pages served over https (openaudiovisual.com, an https tunnel) don't try at all: the browser blocks ws:// there, and a published site has no relay beside it. A show that runs a monitor behind TLS passes the address itself, new MonitorFeed({ url: 'wss://…' }).

records.n: Chrome asks about the local network, or about apps on this device
records.x: Chrome's Local Network Access check puts a permission prompt in front of a public https page that tries to reach your own machine or network; a page served from your machine is not covered (Chrome blog). What it gates, by Chrome version (checked 2026-10-15): Chrome 142: fetch requests (Chrome blog). Chrome 145: two permissions, one for the local network and one for this device itself, called loopback (Chrome Platform Status). Chrome 147: WebSocket and WebTransport connections as well (Chrome Platform Status). Chrome 154: new WebSocket(url, { targetAddressSpace }) lets a page say which kind of address it expects (Chrome Platform Status). When a show runs on openaudiovisual.com or another https site, three things of ours reach for your machine: the OSC bridge (OscOut posts to http://127.0.0.1:7456), the backstage monitor (ws://127.0.0.1:7457) and the Leap bridge. The first time, Chrome asks. If you chose Block, the connection fails, and the console shows net::ERR_BLOCKED_BY_LOCAL_NETWORK_ACCESS_CHECKS (seen on Chrome 154, Leap package notes). What to do: Press Allow. If you blocked it, open the page's site settings (the icon left of the address) and allow it again, then reload. Or open the page from your own machine: node serve.js, then http://localhost:8080/…. That page is not a public site, so Chrome does not ask. This is the safest way to teach or rehearse the OAV → OSC → TouchDesigner path. In an <iframe>, a cross-origin frame needs allow="loopback-network"; a same-origin frame inherits it; a sandboxed frame cannot get it (verified on Chrome 154, Leap package notes). The device check has a button that tries the bridge and the monitor and says which one answered. It connects only when you press it.

records.n: The phone join card says "relay offline"
records.x: On your own machine the phone relay lives inside serve.js (/relay). So the card says "relay offline" when the page was opened from a file, or from a server that is not node serve.js: run the show with node serve.js and open it from there. On a static host (openaudiovisual.com, GitHub Pages) the show uses the public relay instead and the card reads relay ok · … · public relay with a QR code. If it says can't reach the relay (wss://remote.cheyuwu.com/relay) — retrying: the network blocks WebSockets (some school and office Wi-Fi does): try a phone hotspot, or run node serve.js on a laptop on the same network as the phones; the public relay is busy or down: it limits each address to 24 connections and 30 new connections a minute, which a whole classroom behind one router can hit. Run your own (node packages/relay/server.js) and open the show with ?relay=wss://your.host/relay; ?relay=off is in the URL, which turns the remote off (the card is not drawn). The phone opens the link in the QR code, which carries the room and the relay. If the phone says it is connected but nothing moves, check that both show the same #room and that the computer's page was not reloaded into a new room (the room is kept per browser, so another browser or a private window gets a different one).

Run the device check first: it tells you whether this browser has Web MIDI at all. Use Chrome or Edge. Safari has no Web MIDI (WebKit bug 107250, still open), and Firefox has it only after you install its site-permission add-on (Firefox 108). More in Which browser. Allow MIDI when the browser asks. Since Chrome 124 it asks for any MIDI use (Chrome blog). The permission is per site: allowing it on localhost:8080 does not allow it on localhost:3000. The device was plugged in after the page loaded: it should appear by itself. If it does not, reload. Check the L1 · Input panel: a device with its box unticked is muted. Another program may hold the port exclusively (some DAWs and drivers on Windows do). Close it.

records.n: A DAW on the IAC bus is not heard
records.x: By default the Midi engine ignores every input whose name contains IAC (filterOut: 'IAC'). A show that sends MIDI out through the macOS IAC bus would otherwise hear its own output and loop. createShow() uses that default. To receive from a DAW over IAC, turn the built-in engine off and make your own: jsCopy Your engine publishes into the same signals, so routes and worlds work unchanged. (The console's device list and MIDI meter only follow the engine createShow() made.) Do not send MIDI out to the same IAC bus you listen to. A second guard needs no setting: a message that arrives on any input within 40 ms of an identical one the engine just sent is taken for the echo and dropped (new Midi({ echoWindow }), 0 turns it off, midi.echoDropped counts them).

records.n: The DAW went silent after a cable was pulled
records.x: It should not any more. When the output port is unplugged Midi moves to the next best live port, prints one line in the MIDI log and one in the browser console (MIDI out: switched to "…" ("…" was unplugged)), and the L1 · Input panel's MIDI out → row follows. When the port you chose is plugged in again the output goes back to it. If the line says no output left, nothing is plugged in: messages are dropped until a port appears. Choose your port with midi.selectOutput(name) (or enable(name)) so it is the one that returns, and add new Midi({ prefer: ['IAC'] }) to say which port stands in first.

records.n: With two controllers, a route reacts to both
records.x: With two or more MIDI inputs, each device publishes under its own name (midi/<slug>/cc/74) and under the shared legacy name (midi/cc/74). A route on midi/cc/74 hears every device; change its source to the per-device name. The slugs are shown in the L1 · Input panel.

Tick keyboard above the piano first. Capture is off by default so that typing never fights the console's hotkeys. Then A W S E D F T G Y H U J K O L P ; play, Z/X change octave. While keyboard is ticked the letters belong to the piano, so the console's R (reset), T (prompter) and F (fullscreen) do nothing: T and F are piano keys, and an accidental R must not rewind a show you are playing. Space, the arrows and Esc still work, and Esc leaves capture.

Learn binds the first signal that moves by 5% of its range, or the first pulse of any kind. The simulated performer and the drum machine send pulses all the time. Untick simulate performance, stop the drum machine, then click learn again. Remove the wrong route with ✕ in L2 · Mapping.

records.n: The timeline no longer moves a param
records.x: A touched slider or a mapped signal overrides the param, and overrides are sticky: the score yields to the human. Clear it with ✕ next to the param (or show.params.clearOverride(key); clearAllOverrides() for all). A smoothed route keeps writing after its signal arrived, even when muted; remove the route to give the param back to the timeline. See Overrides and the timeline.

records.n: I changed a route in code and nothing changed
records.x: The mapper saved yesterday's routes in localStorage, and a saved source → target pair wins over the declared one (new pairs are still added). Clear the profile, or pass profile: false while you develop: jsCopy

records.n: A route to sound/cutoff only moves between 0 and 1
records.x: outMin/outMax default to the target's range when the route is added, and in createShow() declared routes are added before the sound engine registers its sound/* params. Give the range explicitly: { source: 'midi/cc/74', target: 'sound/cutoff', outMin: 100, outMax: 8000 }.

records.n: The camera or microphone does not start
records.x: The page must be a secure context: http://localhost or https://. A LAN address over plain http:// (http://192.168.1.20:8080) is blocked. The 🎤 mic, 🖐 hands and 🕺 body buttons must be clicked; nothing starts on its own. A button that reads ✗ retry failed: the reason is in the browser's devtools console. On macOS, the browser itself needs camera and microphone access in System Settings → Privacy & Security. Hands and body load MediaPipe and its model from jsDelivr and Google's storage the first time. Offline, they cannot start.

Browsers start audio only after a click. Press 🔊 enable sound in the L4 · Output — sound panel. The Tone.js engine is loaded from jsDelivr at that moment, so the first time needs a network connection. The piano loads about 2 MB of samples the first time you pick it: the picker shows the progress, and the previous instrument keeps playing until the piano is ready. The drum machine's kit starts on the first hit after you tick drum machine.

records.n: A p5.js sketch with the one line misbehaves
records.x: oav-p5 says what went wrong on the page: a card beside the 🎹, in the browser's language, with what happened, why and what to press (When something goes wrong). 🎹 → 🩺 puts the version, the microphone, MIDI, sound, the drums and the wiring on one card: screenshot it when you ask for help. The common ones: knob1 is not defined: the line did not load (offline, or a typo in the URL). It goes first in the sketch, above setup(). Silence: browsers play audio only after the page has been clicked, and a key on a MIDI keyboard does not count. Click the canvas once; until then the 🔊 on the 🎹 button is yellow. The drums are late on a Bluetooth speaker (0.15–0.25 s): ?oav_drumlatency=200 sets the delay by hand, in milliseconds. The video is WebM: Firefox and older Chrome cannot write MP4, and Instagram does not take WebM. Record in Chrome 126 or later, Edge or Safari. The microphone stays at 0 in a sketch embedded in another page: its <iframe> needs allow="microphone" (and allow="midi" for a hardware controller).

records.n: Strudel does not hear OAV Virtual MIDI
records.x: OAV was loaded after Strudel's midin() ran, so midin('OAV Virtual MIDI') gets nothing and says nothing. Put await import('https://openaudiovisual.com/p5/oav-p5.js') in Strudel's settings → prebake (single quotes), save and reload: the prebake runs before your code. Until then 🩺 says "no program has asked OAV Virtual MIDI for MIDI". More in With Strudel.

records.n: The phone's tilt and knocks do nothing on an iPhone
records.x: iOS only gives motion sensors to https:// pages, and only after a tap on 開始 (start). Over plain http:// on the LAN, touch, keys and the control surface still work. Reach serve.js through an HTTPS tunnel for sensors. If the permission was denied once, iOS keeps saying no until you change it in Settings → Safari → Motion & Orientation Access, then reload.

records.n: After a deploy, the site still runs old code
records.x: GitHub Pages lets browsers cache JavaScript for hours while HTML expires in minutes, so a visitor can get new HTML with old modules. Before deploying, run node tools/stamp-version.mjs: it appends ?v=<commit> to module URLs in the examples, packages and homepage. Locally this never happens: serve.js sends Cache-Control: no-store.

records.n: The show slows down when the window is in the background
records.x: Browsers pause requestAnimationFrame in hidden tabs. The Loop then keeps running from a Web Worker at about 15 frames per second, so the timeline, mapped signals and the backstage feed continue, but rendering is slower. Keep the projection window visible, on its own screen, in fullscreen (F).

records.n: An example from a CDN works online but not offline
records.x: p5 (examples 05, 06), Tone.js (sound), MediaPipe (hands, body) and the WebToe app (example 04) come from the network. For an offline venue, download them and point the script tags, the import map or the module options (toneEngine({ cdn }), webtoeWorld({ app })) at local copies.

records.n: The port is already in use
records.x: node serve.js 8081 serves on another port, and the OSC bridge takes one too: node packages/osc/bridges/osc-bridge.js 7470 (then new OscOut('http://127.0.0.1:7470')). The backstage monitor is the exception: a createShow() page always streams to port 7457 on its own host, so free that port. Only a hand-assembled show can point elsewhere, with new MonitorFeed({ url: 'ws://host:7460' }) and node packages/monitor/server.js 7460.
Guiding rule: the framework only grows features that a real show demanded. (This is how the core was born — every module here drove an actual performance before it was generalized.)

four layers: input (midi/audio/chord/pose) → mapping → world → output timeline with scenes, negative standby time, cue hook director's console + performance mode backstage monitor (zero-dep WS relay, LAN devices) OSC bridge; MIDI out with observable throat + panic tests for all pure logic (chord, timeline, mapping, params) mapping profile import/export UI (JSON file, drag-and-drop, ?map=<url>, remembered per world) example: audio-reactive world driven by a live instrument (mic) — 06-cylinder-earth drum machine with analyzer-shaped signals (@openav/drums) on-screen MIDI controllers that mirror real hardware (@openav/midi, example 09) a documentation site: openaudiovisual.com/docs oav-p5: one line for any p5.js sketch, with controllers, a phone, the microphone, sound, a drum machine you can write as one line of rhythm, bars and cues, and video recording; versioned on its own (changelog) one line of rhythm, TidalCycles/Strudel-style mini-notation (@openav/pattern) values over time as TouchDesigner's CHOPs shape them: lag, envelope, speed, spring, trail (@openav/chop) next to Strudel: what a program plays into OAV Virtual MIDI, an external MIDI clock, and link=<room> across tabs and computers (With Strudel)

Audience-device input — classic controller shipped (@openav/relay, @openav/surface, @openav/remote): a zero-dep room server, phone/{id}/* sensors, a TouchOSC-style widget set, layout JSON, autoSurface(params), feedback to the phone. Next: QR code on the join card (@openav/remote/qr, a ~150-line zero-dep encoder) — and on static hosts the show uses the public relay with a random room, so the examples on openaudiovisual.com take phones too experimental surfaces: gesture/physics widgets, shared multi-user surfaces, audience-mode (many phones → aggregate signals like crowd/tilt/mean) mic as a phone sensor; per-device profiles; layout editor / import-export UI Score & Director — shipped (@openav/score): cuts as segment lengths, derived versions, cues, hold, segment modules that fail alone, the prompter's acts, score → MIDI markers. Next: MIDI clock in: MidiClock (@openav/midi) follows start, stop and song position, and oav-p5's drum machine and drumPhase follow it (0.7) the score on an external clock, and clock and transport out, so a DAW can be the master clock of the score, or follow it a clocks table in the cut, only if a show needs engines on two different time lines (see Score & Director) a score editor on the desk: drag a segment's length, see every cue move Signal recording & replay — MIDI takes shipped (@openav/record: TakeRecorder, TakePlayer, .mid in and out; EventLog already records any signal beside a video). Next: replay the full signal stream (hands, body, audio analysis) into any world. Rehearse without the performer; archive the gesture, not just the video. npm publish of @openav/*, and docs pages that are themselves performable with the framework. WebGPU world adapter as WebGPU compute matures for particle/agent worlds.

NDI gateway: headless-browser → NDI bridge so browser output enters professional video pipelines (research: WebRTC→NDI converters already exist). Distributed performance: multi-browser signal sync over WebRTC data channels — several machines, one signal space, geographically split ensembles. Agent performers: LLM-driven agents subscribing to signals and writing params — improvising alongside humans (lineage: The Last Input's autonomous city agents).

a node-based visual editor (cables.gl does this well; we are a library) a synthesis toolkit of our own (Tone.js is the neighbor: @openav/sound wraps it behind a small engine contract, and audio.input() accepts its nodes) being a platform: your show is your repo, not an account on our server

open-audiovisual（OAV）是一套在瀏覽器裡跑的 JavaScript 框架，給現場影音表演用。它只用原生的 ES module：不用建置、沒有相依套件、不用註冊帳號。把 repo clone 下來，跑一個檔案，打開一個網頁，就可以開始了。 每一場演出都要從頭重做的那一塊，由它來處理：MIDI 的底層接線、把輸入變成參數、有場景的時間軸、導演控台、給演奏者的演出模式，以及給舞台監督的後台頁面。你只要寫世界，也就是作品本身。框架的介紹、一台即時在跑的樂器，還有二十六件範例作品，都在首頁。
演奏者用 MIDI 鍵盤、麥克風、鏡頭、手機或螢幕鋼琴來彈範例，從控台操作一場演出。 寫程式的人大約二十行就能寫好一個世界，呼叫一次 createShow()，輸入、映射、時間軸、控台、聲音和後台就都有了。 AI 代理先讀 AGENTS.md，接上 repo 內附的 MCP 伺服器，在一個已經能跑的底盤裡寫世界。見給 AI 代理。
text複製 每一層只做一件事，各有一份寫明的介面約定（架構），所以換掉任何一層，都不用動到其他層。能一直這樣，靠的是兩條規則，寫在核心概念。

框架的核心是從 《The Last Input 終局之前》（吳哲宇，2026）抽出來的。那是台北 IRCAM 聲鬥陣 × C-LAB 台灣聲響實驗室駐村的一場演出，鋼琴和一個活著的數位世界同台，喇叭穹頂有 49.4 聲道。時間軸、和弦語意、多對多的 MIDI learn、OSC 批次傳送，都先撐過一整場十四個場景的真實演出，才在這裡整理成通用的框架。從那之後就定了一條規則：真實演出要求過的功能，框架才長。 映射層的想法，承接 libmapper 對訊號命名空間的研究。姊妹專案 WebToe 是節點式的資料流引擎，可以匯入 TouchDesigner 專案。WebToe 是引擎，open-audiovisual 是演出。
第一次來：先讀快速開始，再讀核心概念，然後是寫一個世界。 要做一場演出：輸入、映射、演出控制、手機、中繼與控制面板。 要查東西：訊號一覽和套件一覽。 出問題了：疑難排解。 這裡寫的每一件事，都對照過 packages/ 裡的原始碼。這一頁和程式碼對不上時，以程式碼為準，那就是這一頁的 bug，請開一個 issue。

挑一個最接近你手上東西的。越往下，東西越大。 在 p5.js 草圖裡加一行。 任何一份 p5.js 草圖（OpenProcessing、p5 編輯器、你自己的網頁）在最前面加一行，就能用 MIDI 控制器、螢幕上的控制器或手機來彈。讀 p5.js 一行接上，再玩帶著這一行的草圖： 範例 15。同一行還能出聲音、開一台能用一行字寫節奏的鼓機、聽麥克風、錄成影片，每一樣在範例裡都有一份現成的草圖（16 到 26）。 在網頁裡放一台控制器。 <oav-controller profile="akai-lpd8"> 把一台能彈的控制器放進任何網頁。讀 MIDI 控制器與嵌入，到控制器圖鑑挑你的那一台。 一整場演出。 一個世界加上一次 createShow() 呼叫，輸入、映射、時間軸、控台、聲音和後台就一起組好。從 範例 01 開始，接著往下讀。

你需要 Node.js（目前任何一個版本都可以，CI 用 Node 22 跑測試）和一個瀏覽器。不用安裝任何東西：沒有 npm install，也沒有打包工具。 bash複製 serve.js 是關掉快取的靜態檔案伺服器（在舞台上跑到舊的程式碼，是一場惡夢），也在 ws://<host>:8080/relay 開好給手機用的中繼。想換連接埠，就把埠號傳進去：node serve.js 3000。這些指令也都寫成了 npm script： 指令實際執行的是 npm startnode serve.js npm run monitornode packages/monitor/server.js，後台監看，連接埠 7457 npm run bridgenode packages/osc/bridges/osc-bridge.js，OSC → UDP 橋接，連接埠 7456 npm testnode --test tests/*.test.js 打開 http://localhost:8080/examples/01-hello-particles/。每個範例都不需要硬體就能跑。

不確定你這台裝置能做什麼？打開裝置體檢。它會看你的瀏覽器、Web MIDI、麥克風、鏡頭和繪圖能力，每一項都告訴你怎麼辦。按了按鈕才會開始，也不會把任何東西送出裝置。 Web MIDI 是各瀏覽器差最多的一項（出處查證於 2026-10-15）： Chrome 和 Edge 有。演出請用它們。從 Chrome 124 起，任何 MIDI 的使用都會問你要不要允許；以前只有系統專用（system-exclusive）才問（Chrome 部落格）。 Firefox 桌面版從 108 版起有 Web MIDI，但要先裝 Firefox 的網站權限附加元件（Firefox 108 版本說明）。 Safari（Mac、iPhone、iPad）沒有 Web MIDI（caniuse）。WebKit 把它列為不實作，理由是指紋辨識的疑慮（WebKit），bug 107250 至今還開著、沒人認領。iPhone 和 iPad 上的 Chrome 底層也是 WebKit，所以一樣沒有。Mac 上有第三方的 Safari 擴充 Safari-WebMIDI，我們沒有實測。 瀏覽器沒有 Web MIDI 的時候，有三條路： 直接在螢幕上彈。 圖鑑裡每一台控制器都能用手指彈，事件照常觸發。 把手機當控制器。 見手機、中繼與控制面板。 iPad 上的瀏覽器 App。 MIDIWeb Browser 是第三方 App（iOS 17.6 以上），讓網頁用得到 Web MIDI。我們沒有拿它跟 open-audiovisual 一起實測。 Windows 11 內建的 Windows MIDI Services（2026-02-17 釋出）讓各程式共用 MIDI 埠並附有 loopback，從瀏覽器送 MIDI 到 DAW 不必再裝 loopMIDI（Windows 部落格）；見用它彈你的 DAW。 不管哪個瀏覽器，還有兩條規則： 鏡頭和麥克風只在安全環境（secure context）裡能用：http://localhost 或 https://。在跑 serve.js 的那台電腦上，請用 localhost 打開演出，不要用它的區域網路位址。 手機在區域網路裡用一般的 http:// 連進來，就能用觸控、琴鍵和控制面板。iOS 只把動作感測器和鏡頭開放給 https:// 頁面（見手機、中繼與控制面板）。

範例頁面分成兩部分：左邊是舞台（世界畫在這裡），右邊是側邊面板。側邊面板由上到下是： 鋼琴，附兩個核取方塊：keyboard（電腦鍵盤擷取）讓你用電腦鍵盤彈，simulate performance（模擬演奏）讓一位模擬演奏者自己彈，不用你動手。 播放控制：播放／暫停、上一個／下一個場景、重設、時鐘、目前的場景，以及一條拖曳軸，每個場景占一格。 Layers（各層狀態）：每一層現在在做什麼（每個輸入每秒幾個事件、啟用中的路由、世界和 FPS、哪些東西正從瀏覽器送出去）。 L1 · Input（輸入）：MIDI 裝置（取消勾選就把那台靜音），以及要點一下才會啟用的來源按鈕：🎤 mic（麥克風）、🖐 hands（手）、🕺 body（身體）。 L2 · Mapping（映射）：每一條路由，附一個靜音核取方塊，按 ✕ 刪除。 L3 · Params（參數）：每個參數一支推桿，按 ✕ 清除覆寫，按 learn 建立映射。 L4 · Output — sound（輸出：聲音），演出有聲音時才會出現：按 🔊 enable sound（開啟聲音）。 Signals（訊號）：每個訊號一個即時儀表。 點面板標題就能收合。 按鍵動作 Space播放／暫停時間軸 ← →上一個／下一個場景 R停止，並把時間軸倒回 0:00 T演出模式（提詞畫面） F全螢幕 M顯示／隱藏螢幕上的 MIDI 控制器（演出設定了 modules.midi.controllers 才有）

螢幕鋼琴：用滑鼠點或手指按琴鍵，在琴鍵上一路拖過去就是刮奏。 電腦鍵盤：先勾選 keyboard（預設不擷取，免得字母鍵搶走控台的快捷鍵）。A W S E D F T G Y H U J K O L P ; 這幾個鍵，從鋼琴的基準音開始，依序彈出相差半音的 17 個音。Z／X 換八度，按住 Shift 會彈得比較大聲。 模擬演奏：模擬演奏者在五聲音階裡隨興地彈，有級進、跳進、三和弦和休止，你只要看映射怎麼跟著起伏。 鼓機（範例 03 和 06）：一台步進音序器，送出的訊號跟麥克風偵測鼓點時送出的長得一樣。 螢幕上的 MIDI 控制器（範例 09）：畫面上是一台市售的控制器，可以用滑鼠彈（支援的裝置列在控制器頁面）。接上實體的那一台，畫面就跟著你的手一起動。 這些送出的訊號都跟真實硬體一樣，所以下游分不出差別。
世界就是一個物件，裡面有 params 和四個生命週期函式。把它交給 createShow()，演出的其他部分就會圍著它組起來： js複製 彈一個音：圓圈會跳大，再慢慢縮回去。拖動 size 推桿，或按旁邊的 learn，再轉一顆旋鈕。整個模型就是這樣：連續控制用參數，事件用訊號。

把 examples/01-hello-particles/ 複製成 examples/<nn>-<name>/（用下一個還沒用的編號）。它的 index.html 已經替每個 @openav/* 套件寫好 import map。那些 ?v= 後綴是快取戳記，部署前由 tools/stamp-version.mjs 寫進去。 在 main.js 寫你的世界（寫一個世界）。 改掉 index.html 裡的 <title>。如果你用 p5 或其他繪圖工具，也在這裡加上 CDN 的 script 標籤。 打開 http://localhost:8080/examples/<nn>-<name>/。 第 1–2 步，AI 代理可以用 MCP 工具 scaffold_world 一次做完（給 AI 代理）。

npm test 通過（測的是純邏輯：和弦、時間軸、映射、中繼、控制面板、MIDI 解析與裝置設定檔、網站頁面）。 頁面載入時，主控台沒有錯誤。只有一則訊息是預期中的：如果後台監看沒在跑，瀏覽器會回報 ws://localhost:7457 拒絕連線。頁面會自己默默重試，間隔越拉越長（最長 30 秒）。跑 npm run monitor，這則訊息就不會再出現。 按 Space：時間軸開始播放，畫面裡有東西隨時間改變。 勾選 keyboard，按 A：不接任何硬體，世界也會有反應。 開發者工具主控台裡的 window.openav 就是整場演出（signals、params、mapper、timeline…），可以自己動手戳戳看。
六個詞撐起整套框架：訊號、參數、路由、世界、時間軸、演出。這一章一個一個講清楚，最後講把它們綁在一起的兩條規則。

訊號（signal）是一個有名字的數值，告訴你現在發生了什麼：一顆旋鈕的位置、房間裡的音量、手腕的高度、上一個和弦的協和度。每個輸入套件都把訊號發布到同一個登錄表（@openav/core 的 Signals），除此之外什麼都不做。訊號是輸入唯一的通用貨幣。 訊號有兩種： 種類存放的是範例讀取方式 連續目前的值，通常在 0..1 之間midi/cc/74 = 0.42signals.get(name)、signals.norm(name) 脈衝最近一次事件帶的內容midi/note/on → { note: 60, vel: 0.8, … }signals.on(name, cb) 名稱是路徑，來源放最前面：midi/cc/74、audio/band/low、pose/hand/right/y、phone/ab12/tilt/x、surface/main/hue。只要在演出上說得通，範圍都會正規化，y 軸也會翻過來，讓 1 代表舉高。你拿到的絕不會是原始的像素值。 宣告訊號時要帶上範圍，儀表和 learn 才知道怎麼縮放它： js複製 對一個沒人宣告過的名稱呼叫 set()，會當場把它定義成 0..1 的連續訊號。如果你的數值落在別的範圍（角度、MIDI 音高編號），請先宣告範圍。 一顆旋鈕、一隻舉起的手、一個和弦的協和度，在這個登錄表裡平起平坐。正因為這樣，你才能把它們混著用：旋鈕做得到的，手也做得到。

參數（param）是世界在聽的數值：hue、bloom、gravity。參數由世界自己宣告，每個參數是一行 schema： js複製 每一格畫面，每個參數都會解析成一個數字： text複製 覆寫會黏住（sticky）。一旦有手或路由碰過 bloom，時間軸就不再推動它，直到你清掉覆寫（在控台按 ✕，或呼叫 params.clearOverride('bloom')）。這跟舞台上一樣：人一伸手接管，樂譜就讓位。 完整的欄位列表在寫一個世界。

路由（route）把一個訊號接到一個參數。路由就是單純的資料： js複製 映射器（mapper，@openav/mapping）收著所有路由，也負責套用：讀取訊號，夾進一個範圍（inMin..inMax），需要的話反轉，用曲線彎折，縮放到參數的範圍，有指定的話再隨時間做平滑。一個訊號可以推動好幾個參數，一個參數也可以聽好幾個訊號。learn 會綁定下一個動起來的訊號，旋鈕和揮動的手都適用。路由可以序列化成 JSON，所以一套接線就是一個檔案，可以帶到下一個場地。細節：映射。
世界（world）就是作品：一個物件，裡面有名稱、參數，以及 init、update、render、dispose。它每一格讀已解析的參數，遇到離散事件也可以直接訂閱訊號。要怎麼畫由它自己決定，2D canvas、p5、three.js、WebToe 節點網路、DOM 都可以，框架不管。細節：寫一個世界。
時間軸（timeline，@openav/timeline）就是樂譜：每個參數的關鍵影格自動化，加上一串場景，每個場景附標題和給演奏者的備註。時間歸它管，世界從來不讀時鐘。場景可以排在 0 秒之前，當作開演前的待命。細節：演出控制。
演出（show）就是一個世界，加上呼叫一次 createShow()（@openav/show）。這一呼叫會建好訊號登錄表、參數、舞台、時間軸、映射器、你要的輸入、聲音、控台、後台資料流和畫面迴圈，然後全部回傳給你。每個範例都是一個世界加上這次呼叫，所以框架長出新模組時，每場演出只要宣告一下就能用。 js複製

框架的每個部分能自由組合，靠的是這兩條規則。每條都有兩種說法，一種講系統怎麼設計，一種講寫程式的人因此要守什麼。 1. 訊號是輸入唯一的通用貨幣。所以：連續控制走參數，離散事件可以直接用訊號。 假設一個世界在 update() 裡直接讀 signals.get('midi/cc/74')，今天配上你的控制器還是能跑，但時間軸、舞者的手腕、手機或別人的控制器，就再也演奏不了它。你等於把這場演出焊死在一個輸入上。改成宣告一個參數，讓一條路由接上 midi/cc/74 → yourParam。這樣同一個世界誰都能用，控台、手機控制面板和 learn 也都看得到這個參數。 事件就不一樣了。「按下一個音」「一個和弦解決了」「大鼓打了一下」都是瞬間，不是持續的數值。在 init() 裡訂閱它們是對的，我們也鼓勵這麼做。世界能對你反應，靠的就是這些事件，少了它們，世界只會自己飄。 2. 世界永遠不知道誰在演奏它。所以：外殼永遠不知道作品是什麼。 世界讀的是參數，數值來自時間軸、MIDI 旋鈕、舞者還是推桿，它看不見。框架也一樣：不要為了讓某個範例好看去改 packages/*。改框架，就要讓每件作品都變好。換作品，就是換掉世界和它的資料，外殼留著不動。
open-audiovisual 是一套資料層框架。它的價值全在一件事：四層和兩條主軸分得乾乾淨淨，換掉其中任何一個，都不用碰到其他部分。這一章把每一層的介面約定講清楚。

整套系統由一個 Loop（@openav/core）帶著跑。下面是 createShow() 每一格的執行順序（packages/show/index.js）： js複製 訊號在兩格之間進來，裝置或 socket 什麼時候觸發，就什麼時候到。沒有平滑的路由會立刻寫入參數，有平滑的路由則是設一個目標值，由 mapper.update(dt) 慢慢滑過去。createShow() 不包含 OSC 輸出，要用的話，在 onFrame 裡呼叫 flush 送出（見演出控制）。 dt 以秒為單位，上限夾在 0.1（new Loop(fn, { maxDt })），所以就算卡頓，世界也不會爆掉。瀏覽器凍結 requestAnimationFrame 的時候（例如投影視窗被切到背景），一個 Web Worker 心跳會讓迴圈繼續跑，大約每 66 ms 一次（約每秒 15 格）。有人切了視窗，時間軸、映射中的訊號和後台資料流也不能停。 參數解析的順序（整個設計的核心）： text複製 覆寫會黏住：一旦有旋鈕碰過 bloom，時間軸就不再推動它，直到你清掉覆寫（在控台按 ✕）。這跟演出現場一樣：人一伸手接管，樂譜就讓位。

介面約定：輸入套件把有名字、經過正規化的訊號發布到 Signals 登錄表，除此之外什麼都不做。它們從不碰參數或世界。 名稱像路徑：midi/cc/74、chord/consonance、pose/hand/right/y 連續訊號宣告 {min, max}，隨時都有一個目前值 脈衝訊號（kind: 'pulse'）觸發事件，帶的內容就是事件物件 誰都可以訂閱：signals.on(name, cb) 或 signals.onAny(cb) 新增一種輸入方式（呼吸感測器、遊戲手把、股票報價、天氣 API），就是寫一個呼叫 signals.set()／signals.pulse() 的 class。下游什麼都不用改。重點就在這裡。 現有的輸入：@openav/midi（硬體與螢幕上的控制器）、keys、drums、audio（麥克風）、pose（鏡頭看身體與手）、leap（Leap Motion／Ultraleap 的手），以及經由 remote 和 surface 的手機。瀏覽器自己打不開的硬體，透過一支講網頁協定的本機小橋接程式進來（leap 的橋接在 ws://127.0.0.1:6437）；瀏覽器這一側仍然只是一個發出訊號的 class。 分析器位在原始來源和映射之間：@openav/chord 訂閱 midi/note/on|off，再發布 chord/*。對映射器來說，它還是一個輸入，只是它聽的是別的訊號，沒有直接接裝置。

介面約定：把訊號接到參數的，只有它一個。路由就是資料： js複製 多對多：一個訊號可以推動好幾個參數，一個參數也可以聽好幾個訊號（以最後寫入的為準）。learn 只會新增路由，從不取代。 learn 是廣義的 MIDI learn：mapper.learn('bloom') 會綁定下一個動了至少自身範圍 5% 的訊號，旋鈕和揮動的手都算數。 路由可以序列化成 JSON → 映射設定檔就是可以分享的檔案。 完整說明：映射。

介面約定：世界（World）是 { name, params, init, update(dt, state, io), render, dispose }。它讀 state（已解析的參數值）。它可以為了離散事件訂閱訊號（一個 note-on 生出一顆粒子，是事件，不是參數），但連續控制一定要經過參數，不然時間軸和其他輸入就再也演奏不了你的世界。 舞台（Stage）管生命週期和參數彙整，刻意不管繪圖。p5、three.js、2D canvas、SVG、DOM 都可以，框架不插手。 憲法級的規則（承襲自《The Last Input 終局之前》）：外殼永遠不知道作品是什麼。 換作品＝換掉世界＋自動化資料。外殼留著。 完整說明：寫一個世界。

records.n: L4 · 輸出：影像與聲音兩條分支，都是選用
records.x: 輸出層分成兩條分支。兩條都接在同一條「訊號 → 映射 → 參數」主軸上：聲音是一種可以演奏的狀態，不是附帶的效果。 影像分支 螢幕是預設的輸出。演出模式（T）給演奏者一個提詞畫面，觀眾看的是全螢幕的舞台視窗（F）。 錄製（@openav/record）：作品和演奏者的鏡頭合成進一張尺寸精確的畫布（直式 1080×1920 到 4K），跟作品自己的聲音交給同一個 MediaRecorder 錄，畫面和聲音用的是同一個時鐘。MIDI 錄音則把演奏本身錄下來，再播回演出裡。 未來：NDI 閘道（見路線圖，基礎工作在姊妹專案 WebToe 裡）。 聲音分支 MIDI 輸出（外接合成器、DAW）：midi.send()/noteOn()/cc()，所有訊息走同一個出口，而且看得到（onSend），儀表能顯示每一則送出的訊息。另外有一個真的派得上用場的 panic()。 頁面內合成：@openav/sound，一份精簡、可抽換的引擎介面約定（params, enable, noteOn, noteOff, set, dispose），先支援 Tone.js 引擎（從 CDN 載入，按下 enable 才載）。這個引擎彈的是登記好的樂器：取樣的平台鋼琴、敲擊琴、弦樂、風琴、合成器音色，一個檔案一種聲音，在控台上挑。引擎的參數註冊成 sound/*，旋鈕、手或時間軸演奏濾波器截止頻率的方式，跟演奏畫面完全一樣。@openav/drums 的鼓組是用同一份介面約定寫的第二個引擎（純 WebAudio，不需要取樣音檔）。 OSC：瀏覽器 → HTTP → osc-bridge.js → UDP（Spat、Reaper、TD、燈光）。每格批次送出，同一個位址在一格裡只留最新的一則訊息。

純邏輯，不碰 DOM：參數＋自動化關鍵影格＋場景 → state(t)。場景可以從負的 t 開始（開演前的待命）。onSceneChange 就是 cue 的掛鉤：聲音、燈光、提示都從這裡觸發。帶 hold: true 的場景，播放到它的結尾就停住，等操作者放行。 有結構的演出，會把總譜（@openav/score）加進這條主軸：把演出寫成各段的長度，由 Score 算出每個起點、終點、cue 和倒數，再由 Director 去執行負責每一段的模組（進一次、出一次，某個模組壞掉只會停用它自己）。時間軸的場景和總長都從總譜來，導演則以參數層的身分接在時間軸上： text複製 總譜只決定什麼時候。實際發生的事，仍然是以參數的形式傳進世界。完整說明見總譜與導演。
演出頁面透過 WebSocket，把 JSON 快照（有節流，約 15 Hz）串流到一個沒有相依套件的中繼（server.js，手寫的 RFC 6455 實作）。區域網路裡任何一支手機或一台筆電，打開後台頁面就能看到：時鐘、場景、世界、FPS、覆寫、每個訊號和參數，還有「舞台畫面斷線」警示。後台監看在框架裡跟其他層一樣重要：沒有後台的演出，只是一場彩排。

控台（@openav/console）：側邊面板裡的導演控台，依層排列（Layers → L1 → L2 → L3 → L4 → Signals），另外還有演出模式。它讀的就是迴圈正在跑的那批物件，自己不保存任何狀態。 手機（@openav/relay、@openav/surface、@openav/remote）：手機和 iPad 透過 WebSocket 中繼加入一個房間，發布 phone/* 和 surface/* 訊號。對映射器來說，它們只是多一個輸入。見手機、中繼與控制面板。
世界是整套框架裡，唯一一定要自己寫的部分。其他都是組裝。
js複製

成員什麼時候執行拿到什麼 name—一個不重複的字串，舞台用這個名字註冊世界 params註冊世界時讀一次參數宣告組成的陣列（見下方） init(ctx)世界啟用時{ container, signals, params }。可以是 async，createShow() 會等它跑完才啟動迴圈 update(dt, state, io)每一影格dt 以秒為單位（≤ 0.1），state 是每個參數的 { key: value }，io 是 { signals, … } render()每一影格，緊接在 update 之後不帶參數，用 update 存下來的東西來畫 dispose()換成另一個世界時釋放 GPU 物件、DOM、訂閱 surface選用手機控制面板的版面。有它的話，modules.remote 直接用它，不再自動產生（手機） container 是一個絕對定位、鋪滿整個舞台的元素。舞台在每次 init 之前都會把它清空，所以你不用收拾別人留下的 DOM。update 或 render 丟出的例外，舞台會接住並記下來（[stage] update:／[stage] render:），演出照常進行。

欄位意義 key路由、自動化和控台用的名字。必填。 label控台上顯示的文字。預設是 key。 min, max範圍。覆寫的值會限制在範圍內，路由也會把訊號縮放到這個範圍。 def沒有自動化、也沒有覆寫時的值。核心只讀 def，只有 autoSurface() 另外看得懂 default。 step覆寫的值會對齊到 step 的倍數。在時間軸上，有 step 的參數會在每個關鍵影格停住，不做內插。 pulse設成 true，它就變成一次性的觸發：控台會顯示 fire（觸發）按鈕，映射過來的脈衝訊號（或一個往上越過 0.5 的連續訊號）會觸發它，世界用 params.onPulse(key, cb) 來聽。脈衝參數在 state 裡沒有值。 group分組用的標籤。聲音引擎的參數用 'sound'。autoSurface() 會替每一組做一頁手機頁面。 options有 step 的參數，每個值各叫什麼名字（['Circle', 'Petal', 'Star']），手機控制面板會把它們顯示成單選按鈕。 surface給手機控制面板的提示：{ type, color, label }。 兩個註冊過的世界如果宣告了同一個 key，就共用同一個參數（以先宣告的為準）。

records.n: 大家最常違反的那條規則
records.x: 連續控制一律走參數。事件可以直接用訊號。 如果你的世界在 update() 裡直接讀 signals.get('midi/cc/74')，它還是會動，至少今天、接你的控制器時會動。但時間軸、舞者、別人的控制器設定檔，就再也推不動它了。你把這場演出焊死在一個輸入上了。改用路由：宣告一個參數，讓映射器接上 midi/cc/74 → yourParam，同一個世界誰來都能演奏。 事件不一樣：「按下一個音」「一個和弦解決了」「打到一次起音」是瞬間，不是持續的量。在 init() 裡訂閱這些事件是對的，我們也鼓勵這樣做。有了這些事件，世界才會回應你，不然它只是被參數推著走。 常用的事件訊號：midi/note/on 和 midi/note/off（任何鍵盤、螢幕鋼琴、模擬演奏者、手機都會發）、chord/event（每一次彈奏做一次分析）、audio/onset、audio/kick、drum/kick。完整清單在訊號一覽。

時間軸跟世界寫在一起，在呼叫 createShow() 時設定： js複製 關鍵影格寫成 [seconds, value]，依時間排序。第一個關鍵影格之前取第一個值，最後一個之後取最後一個值。 場景依 t 排序。title 和 note 是演奏者在演出模式（T）裡讀到的文字，下方還會顯示下一個場景和倒數。 t 為負數的場景，是演出開始前的待命段落：設成 t: -30，時鐘就從 -0:30 開始走。 試著只用時間軸演出你的世界。如果很無聊，就是少了一個參數。 細節見演出控制。
舞台本身不帶渲染器。在 init 裡建一個，在 dispose 裡銷毀。
@openav/stage 的 createCanvas(container, { alpha = false }) 回傳 { canvas, ctx, fit, dispose }。fit() 讓 canvas 跟容器一樣大（裝置像素比最高到 2），回傳以 CSS 像素計的 { w, h }。在 render() 一開頭呼叫它。範例 01、02、03、07、08 和 09 都用它。
在範例的 index.html 用 script 標籤載入 p5，再用 instance mode 跑在容器裡。p5 有自己的繪圖迴圈，所以 update 只負責存下 state，render 留空（範例 05 和 06）： html複製 js複製
內附的範例目前都沒用 three.js，寫法如下。把 three 加進範例的 import map（"three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.160.0/build/three.module.js"），渲染器存在 this 上，所有東西都要 dispose： js複製

@openav/world-webtoe 的 webtoeWorld() 把一張 WebToe 節點網路變成一個世界。節點網路跑在 iframe 裡。哪一格有參數改變，就把算好的參數值傳進 iframe，節點網路裡寫成 ext('name', fallback) 的參數都會收到（範例 04）： js複製 選項：name（預設 'webtoe'）、app（預設 https://webtoe.openaudiovisual.com/）、project、params、extra。
任何東西加進 container 都可以。舞台只負責呼叫你的函式。

records.n: 一場演出裡的多個世界
records.x: js複製 所有世界的參數一開始就會註冊，所以控台和時間軸碰得到每一個世界的參數。那個世界已經啟用的話，stage.activate(name) 什麼都不做。

update(dt, state, io) 會收到 io。用 createShow() 時，io 裡只有 signals。演出建好之後，再把輸出用的物件加上去，每個世界都看得到： js複製 接著在世界裡： js複製 很多時候，直接在組裝演出的程式裡處理會更簡單，範例 05 就是這樣：show.signals.on('midi/note/on', ({ note, vel }) => show.midi?.noteOn(note, Math.round(vel * 127), 1))。要用頁面裡的樂器（平台鋼琴、敲擊琴、弦樂、風琴、合成器音色），請用 modules.sound（演出控制）。
每一個連續控制都是參數（試著只用時間軸演出你的世界） dispose() 會釋放 GPU 物件和事件訂閱（世界會在演出中即時切換） dt 突然變大時，世界撐得住（Loop 會把它限制在 100 ms 以內，但別假設它是 16 ms） 世界裡沒有任何地方直接讀時鐘：時間歸時間軸管 頁面載入時瀏覽器主控台零錯誤，只用螢幕鋼琴也跑得動

每一種輸入只做一件事：發出訊號。用 createShow() 時，在 modules 裡打開需要的輸入就好。每一種輸入也都是普通的類別，可以單獨拿出來用。訊號的確切名稱和範圍，查訊號一覽。 輸入套件modules 的 key預設發出的訊號 MIDI 硬體@openav/midimidi開（設成 false 就關掉）midi/… 螢幕上的 MIDI 控制器@openav/midimidi: { controllers }關midi/<device>/<control> 螢幕鋼琴、電腦鍵盤、模擬演奏者@openav/keyskeys開（設成 false 就移除）midi/note/on、midi/note/off 鼓機@openav/drumsdrums關drum/…，以及第 10 頻道的 midi/note/on 麥克風@openav/audioaudio關audio/… 和弦分析@openav/chordchord關chord/… 身體（鏡頭）@openav/posepose關pose/… 手（鏡頭）@openav/posehands關hand/… 手（Leap Motion）@openav/leapleap關leap/… 手機與 iPad@openav/remoteremote關phone/…、surface/…、midi/note/… 麥克風、鏡頭這類需要權限、或要使用者先點一下才能開的來源，createShow() 會先建好，但要等你在控台的 L1 · Input（輸入）面板按下對應的按鈕，才會開始：🎤 mic（麥克風）、🖐 hands（手）、🕺 body（身體）。

createShow() 啟動時會建立一個 Midi 引擎並呼叫 enable()，所以頁面一打開，瀏覽器可能就會跳出 MIDI 權限的詢問。演出中可以隨時插拔裝置，L1 · Input 面板會列出它們，取消勾選某一台就能把它靜音，不用拔線。 每收到一則訊息，都會用兩組名稱發出去： 舊式名稱（legacy，大多數世界用的就是這組，不分頻道）：midi/note/on 和 midi/note/off 脈衝、midi/cc/<n>（0..1）、midi/bend（−1..1）。 分頻道：midi/ch/<ch>/cc/<n>、midi/ch/<ch>/note/<n>（按住時是 0..1 的力度，放開時為 0）、midi/ch/<ch>/bend、midi/ch/<ch>/pressure、midi/ch/<ch>/poly/<n>。 note-on 帶的內容是 { note, vel, velocity, ch, device }：vel 是 0..1，velocity 是原始的 1..127，ch 是 1..16，device 是連接埠的 slug。 接了兩台以上的裝置時，每一台還會用自己的 slug 另外發一份，控制項才不會撞名：midi/<slug>/cc/<n>、midi/<slug>/note/on、midi/<slug>/note/off、midi/<slug>/bend。slug 取自連接埠名稱（Arturia MiniLab 3 → arturia-minilab-3，同型號的第二台會加上 -2），所以裝置斷線再接回來，路由還在。舊式名稱也照常發出，所以接在 midi/cc/74 上的路由聽得到每一台裝置。 Clock 訊息直接略過。Program change、transport 和 SysEx 不會發出（框架從不要 SysEx 權限）。 不透過 createShow()，單獨使用： js複製 filterOut 是一個不分大小寫的正規表示式，名稱符合的輸入連接埠一律略過。預設值 'IAC' 把 macOS 的 IAC bus 擋在外面，不然演出透過 IAC 送出 MIDI，又會聽到自己送出的訊息。想從 IAC 接收，請看疑難排解。MIDI 輸出寫在演出控制。

modules: { midi: { controllers: { profile: '<profile id>' } } } 會在螢幕上放一張已知控制器的圖。接上那台控制器，畫面就跟著你的手一起動，沒接的話，用滑鼠或手指直接在畫面上彈。它的控制項會發出 midi/<device>/<control> 這類名稱，controllerRoutes() 幫你寫好接到參數的路由。設定檔（profile）、怎麼 learn 不認識的裝置、LED 回饋和嵌入，都在MIDI 控制器與嵌入這一章。支援的裝置列在控制器頁面。

records.n: 螢幕鋼琴、電腦鍵盤與模擬演奏者
records.x: @openav/keys 預設開啟。它會在控台上方放一台鋼琴，附兩個核取方塊：keyboard（電腦鍵盤擷取）和 simulate performance（模擬演奏）。選項（modules.keys）：base（最低音，預設 48）、octaves（預設 2）、sim（是否顯示模擬演奏的核取方塊，預設 true）、capture（是否顯示 keyboard 核取方塊，預設 true）。 它發出 midi/note/on { note, vel, ch: 0 } 和 midi/note/off { note, ch: 0 }。注意跟硬體不同：ch 是 0，而且沒有 velocity 和 device 欄位。只讀 note 和 vel 的世界，兩種都能用。 電腦鍵盤（勾選 keyboard 之後）：A W S E D F T G Y H U J K O L P ; 從 base 開始，依序彈出相差半音的 17 個音。Z／X 移動一個八度（base 維持在 24 到 84 之間），按住 Shift 力度加 20。擷取開著的時候，鋼琴會接管所有字母鍵（preventDefault），Space、方向鍵和數字鍵照常交給控台。 模擬演奏者（SimPlayer）在比 base 高一個八度的地方彈五聲音階：大多是級進，偶爾跳進或彈三和弦，中間也會真的停下來。用程式碼控制：show.keys.sim.toggle(true)。 js複製

modules: { drums: true } 會加上一台 16 步、四軌（kick、snare、hat、clap）的音序器，附節奏型（four on floor、breakbeat、half time、latin、sparse）、速度滑桿（60–180 BPM，預設 112）、swing，以及模擬真人手感的時間偏移。勾選 drum machine（鼓機）就開始打。它用自己合成的鼓組發聲（不用取樣音色），發出： drum/kick、drum/snare、drum/hat、drum/clap：脈衝 { level }。 drum/<lane>/env：每一軌一條 0..1 的波封，大約 0.12 秒衰減完，可以直接映射到參數。 midi/note/on { note, vel, ch: 10 }，用 General MIDI 的音高（kick 36、snare 38、clap 39、closed hat 42）。 這些訊號跟麥克風偵測鼓點時發出的長得一樣（audio/kick、audio/kick/env…），所以映射到 kick 的世界分不出真的大鼓和鼓機。範例 06 就把兩者接到同一組參數。選項（modules.drums）：engine（改用另一個聲音引擎）、autoEnableEngine（預設 true：第一下打擊就會啟動鼓組的音訊引擎，不必另外點一下）。
